- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–4 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 75 or below 65), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model misreads momentum; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
